request.spec:
A fourth role, restricted, can be assigned. A restricted user sees on the people list only the
people of the crews they lead or belong to (by a person with the user's name) and that person
themselves: no other row is on the screen. Every other figure (the totals row, the header, the
summary, the periods, the pools) is still over everyone on the sheet.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A fourth role, restricted, can be assigned. A restricted user sees on the people list only the
people of the crews they lead or belong to (by a person with the user's name) and that person
themselves: no other row is on the screen. Every other figure (the totals row, the header, the

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A fourth role, **restricted**, can now be assigned, and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**What a restricted user sees:** the people list shows only the person whose name matches the user, plus the leads and members of every crew that person leads or belongs to. If no person on the sheet has the user's name, the list is empty. The totals row, the header, the summary, the periods and the pools still count everyone on the sheet.

**Changes:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration `V103__restricted_role.sql` lets the role table hold `restricted`.
- **Server:** `restricted` is added to the roles in `Role.java` and is accepted when setting a role in `AccessController.java`.
- **Front end:** the role form in `access.ts` accepts `restricted`. In `people.ts`, a new `visible` set of person ids narrows the listed rows, while the figures are still worked out from the full list.

**Decisions for you:**
- **What a restricted user can do:** the request only says what they see, so I gave them the same rights as a clerk. That means the same permission-matrix rights and the same limit on how much they can settle. Without this, the existing permission checks would have stopped them opening or settling claims (because restricted isn't a clerk), and the settle-limit check would have treated them as having no limit (because it only applies to clerks).
- **The filtering only happens on screen.** The server still sends every person to a restricted user's browser, because all the totals are worked out there from the full list. So the role hides rows but doesn't protect the data. Making it a real access control would mean the server sends only the visible people and works out the totals itself, which is a larger change.
